This issue appeared firstly in the `unity-6` beta branch and then continued to progress in the `open-beta` branch after merging the `unity-6` beta branch after announcing it was ready for merging.

Distribution doesn't matter in this case because fault is the same on different setups and use cases.

I can only suggest (and guess) using the `git bisect` 5 patches before merging `unity-6` into `open-beta` and 2 patches after merging.

Distribution: `Debian Forky/sid`.

Graphical environment: KDE on Wayland.

Steam installation: Non-flatpak.

Proton: 11 RTSP Fork.

SLR: steamrt4.

Architecture: AMD64

All information about the fault has already been sent by the Unity crash handler.

The issue is already in the `release` branch.
I don't actually think it's related to X3D chips anymore. We're getting it consistently on a 3900X (Mint Cinnamon) but not at all on a 5800X3D (Arch KDE Plasma)

Was suffering this issue bad today on a 9950X3D2 with Arch, native Steam, latest kernel & drivers, with any versions of Proton. Couldn't consistently change worlds, open menus, or stay in a world for too long before getting the SuspendThread crash.

Disabling Esync and Fsync seemed to fix it for me. Set your VRC launch options to:

PROTON_NO_ESYNC=1 PROTON_NO_FSYNC=1 %command%

This will likely cause a performance hit but I had no crashes in 3 hours after setting this when previously I would crash within minutes. Hoping it helps someone else. Also hoping we get whatever release this fix is coming to soon...

@{5ba8889cfa86f032d1596de2|full_name} This allowed me to use VRChat long enough to go to other worlds and muck around a bit at least. Will give longer test later. Many thanks if this is the silver bullet!

@{5ba8889cfa86f032d1596de2|full_name} This inspired me to check if NTSync is enabled. NTSync is the newer in-kernel replacement for ESync/FSync. It wasn't enabled.

To check: `ls -l /dev/ntsync` (if this file exists it's enabled)

To enable it: `sudo modprobe ntsync`

To enable it on future reboots: `echo ntsync | sudo tee /etc/modules-load.d/ntsync.conf`

With this, I could play for over an hour without issues.
